description: Colour never carries a state or a name alone. (1) The name label of another learner is text on that learner's palette colour: for every palette slot of the presence palette (the 12 base hues and the lighter/darker and desaturated cycles after them) and both appearances, the label's ink must reach the minimum contrast of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 against the slot colour. (2) With forced colours (Windows high contrast) backgrounds, shadows and custom colours are replaced by system colours, so every state the stylesheet shows through one of them needs its own rule inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`: each entry names the state, the selector of that rule and the properties it must declare. (3) The text of every state the challenges add — hints, miss marks, the clock's last 30 and 10 seconds and its end — is the design system's ink (`ink`, a token of the appearance) on the page's ground (`ground`), over which the low-time states lay a tint (`tint`: a palette colour at a share, as `color-mix(in srgb, colour share, transparent)` composites over the ground); the stylesheet paints none of them in a colour of its own, and in both appearances the ink must reach the minimum contrast of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 against the ground with its tint.
